name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platforms: tvOS and visionOS. Shared gallery has 20 objects and details. Current idea treats gaze hover as remote keyboard focus, opens details automatically when looked at and requires pinpoint mouse cursor movement on TV. Focus disappears after returning from detail. Vision Pro interaction requires raised arms for every action.

# Apple HIG: Map user actions to input and alternatives

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the action and available hardware/input context, then enter the keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controller, Pencil, Crown or sensor procedure.
2. Preserve reserved system gestures and familiar input meanings. Separate targeting, focus, selection and activation; define feedback and reachable alternatives for the actions people must complete.
3. Account for comfort, precision, fatigue and switching between available inputs. Custom inputs should not remove an accessible route to an essential action.
4. Deliver an action-to-input mapping, focus/selection states and observable verification scenarios. Keep code/static observations separate from physical comfort, eye/hand and hardware checks.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

## Completion evidence

Report the concrete decisions or changes, their source support, and which checks
passed, failed or were not executed. A source citation or a list of links is not
the requested work product. Retain platform exceptions and unresolved source
conflicts; the absence of a platform subsection does not establish support.

---
name: apple-hig-focus-and-selection
description: Use when designing or reviewing keyboard, remote, or controller focus navigation, persistent selection, directional reachability, or disappearing focused items.
---

# Keep the interaction target distinct from the chosen value

Read [Focus and selection](../../references/focus-and-selection.md). Inspect platform/input, focus groups, selected state, dynamic content, and supplied implementation. Establish design/review/adaptation mode. The guide's component-focus model excludes iOS/watchOS; visionOS gaze hover is a different system.

Map focus movement separately from activation and persistent selection. Focus may select automatically only when that does not unexpectedly shift context; tvOS normally needs separate activation. Use system effects and avoid moving focus without input. If an item disappears during discrete directional movement, choose a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide the indicator rather than inventing the next destination.

On iPad, group custom content so Tab moves among logical groups and arrows move within them in expected reading order; prioritize the likely entry item. Ordinary content focus coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls. On TV, every interactive item needs directional reachability and room for enlarged focus art. Keep unfocused, focused, pressed, selected, and unavailable states distinct. Full-screen gestures should manipulate visible content rather than invisible focus.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a TV watchlist opens each item as focus passes over it and uses the same glow for focus and Saved. Decision: navigation must not activate content, and persistent choice must survive focus movement. After, focus raises/highlights the item, Select opens it, and a filled saved indicator remains as focus moves; unavailable items are inactive and unreachable.

Deliver a focus-route/group map and state contract or implementation. Walk each entry, direction, activation, return, and removal scenario. Fail if a control cannot be reached/exited, focus jumps without input, selected state vanishes with focus, or enlargement obscures information. Source inspection can establish intended grouping; actual focus engines, remote behavior, and Full Keyboard Access need supported execution.

Use [Remotes](../apple-hig-remotes/SKILL.md) for TV button meanings, [Keyboards](../apple-hig-keyboards/SKILL.md) for shortcuts/access, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) when the request actually concerns gaze feedback.

---
name: apple-hig-eyes
description: Use when designing or reviewing visionOS eye-targeted controls, system hover effects, target separation, comfortable gaze shifts, or gaze privacy assumptions.
---

# Offer a clear target without observing private gaze

Read [Eyes](../../references/eyes.md). Inspect target bounds, normal/hover states, content depth, competing movement, and assistive input routes. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. This is visionOS guidance; retain the current stack and separate system hover from connected-keyboard/controller focus.

Choose a recognizable stable target and use standard hover responses where appropriate. Group an image and its label into one containing hover region when they form one action. Check separation using the guide's 16 pt margin or 60 pt center-distance guidance; avoid overlapping feedback. Remove noisy patterns and peripheral movement that pull attention away or create ambiguous depth.

Keep important content in comfortable view without repeated broad eye movement or rapid refocusing. Sustained reading normally belongs at least 1 m away; reserve closer content for brief interaction. Do not invent exact field-of-view dimensions or assume head-pose access outside its platform context.

For custom hover, declare normal/hover appearances and keep a primary visual stable. Use immediate subtle affordance, a short delay for expansion that could interfere with quick action, and a longer delay for optional information. The system applies effects outside the app process: it does not disclose pre-tap gaze or run gaze-dependent business logic. Hover may reveal a predefined favorite affordance, but cannot favorite an item itself. Provide alternative input/assistive routes.

**Before → decision → after:** A gallery marks a work as viewed and enlarges its target into a neighbor whenever someone looks toward it. Decision: hover is private system feedback, not an app event, and targets need stable separation. After, a contained stable artwork/label region receives system hover emphasis; explicit activation opens the work, while any viewed state follows a supported deliberate event.

Deliver corrected target/hover specifications or implementation. Fail if looking alone changes stored content, targets collide, or required interactions have no alternative. Only a worn Vision Pro can establish responsiveness, gaze comfort, and distraction; static geometry cannot.

Use [Spatial layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for depth/anchors and [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for actual keyboard/controller focus.

---
name: apple-hig-remotes
description: Use when designing or reviewing tvOS Siri Remote navigation, deliberate activation, playback/scrubbing, Back behavior, or compatible program-guide buttons.
---

# Preserve deliberate remote actions across browsing and playback

Read [Remotes](../../references/remotes.md). Inspect the TV hierarchy, playback/game state, remote mappings, and requested design/review/adaptation. This is tvOS-specific. Preserve the existing stack and distinguish a remote press from accidental surface contact or movement.

Map swipes to predictable directional focus/scrolling with corresponding feedback; strength can govern scrolling momentum. Use presses for deliberate activation. Avoid acting on taps during live playback because passing or resting a remote can produce them. Press-then-swipe enters scrubbing; preserve the relationship between gesture and visible media position.

Define Back by hierarchy and task state. In ordinary browsing, Back opens the parent, not necessarily the last screen visited; root returns Home. During gameplay, Back may open a pause menu, Back from that menu resumes, and an additional deliberate action can leave for the game menu. Holding Back retains its system Home behavior. Play/Pause must control active media; game-specific secondary/skip use needs appropriate context.

If an electronic program guide exists, guide/browse buttons open it and page buttons navigate it. During playback, those page requests change channels. Without a guide, preserve system routing to the default guide app rather than inventing unrelated meanings.

**Before → decision → after:** A streaming app treats every clickpad tap as Pause and makes Back jump to a recently searched page rather than the show's parent. Decision: accidental touches should not interrupt viewing and hierarchy must remain predictable. After, deliberate Play/Pause controls playback, presses activate, and Back from the episode returns to its show; guide/page behavior follows the active context.

Deliver a state-by-button/gesture mapping and corrected interaction artifact. Walk browse, play, scrub, pause, and return routes. Fail if incidental contact changes playback, Back strands the person or exits unexpectedly, or a program-guide button performs an unrelated action. Actual Siri Remote gestures, momentum, and across-room feedback need hardware testing; keyboard simulation is partial evidence.

Use [Focus and selection](../apple-hig-focus-and-selection/SKILL.md) for directional reachability or [Game controls](../apple-hig-game-controls/SKILL.md) for controller/menu consistency.

---
name: apple-hig-gestures
description: Use when designing, reviewing, or adapting touch, indirect hand, direct spatial, trackpad, or Watch gestures and their discoverable alternatives.
---

# Make gestures predictable shortcuts to visible work

Read [Gestures](../../references/gestures.md). Inspect the task, target platforms, existing system/custom gestures, physical demands, and visible alternatives. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Preserve the stack; use actual interaction evidence to distinguish a gesture conflict from an untested possibility.

Start with standard meanings for tap, swipe, drag, hold, zoom, and rotation. Give immediate predictive feedback showing what moves, how far, and whether movement is locked/unavailable. Keep an explicit route for essential work through controls or supported alternative input. A custom gesture needs a frequent specialized task, simple explanation, discoverability, and another way to perform the action; if teaching it is harder than the task, redesign.

Check conflicts against the platform's reserved navigation, edges, undo/redo, multitasking, and overlay gestures. Do not repurpose a familiar system action to save one button. On visionOS, prioritize indirect interaction from rest and avoid sustained raised arms, complex two-hand/finger patterns, prescribed handedness, or required body movement. Custom hand gestures need Full Space/hand-data permission and must coexist with palm/wrist system overlays. On Watch, double tap already scrolls or advances vertical containers; only assign a primary button action where the container context permits it.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a spatial editor requires a two-hand twist above shoulder height to close a panel and places tool UI directly on the wrist. Decision: dismissal must be simple and compatible with system overlays. After, a labeled Close action and familiar indirect activation cover dismissal; optional manipulation gestures supplement visible controls, and task tools move away from reserved wrist space.

Deliver a gesture-to-action/conflict map and revised interaction artifact. Fail if an essential task has only a complex gesture, standard navigation changes meaning, feedback lags behind the manipulated content, or a system overlay competes for the same movement. Ergonomics and gesture recognition require real-use/device testing; static review cannot verify reliability.

Use [Accessibility](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md) for alternatives, [Apple Pencil and Scribble](../apple-hig-apple-pencil-and-scribble/SKILL.md) for stylus gestures, or [Eyes](../apple-hig-eyes/SKILL.md) for indirect target feedback.

# Focus and selection Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Focus visually identifies an interaction target for component-based navigation with keyboards, remotes, and controllers. Focus can select an item automatically, except where selection would shift context; tvOS normally requires separate activation. Rings/highlights on tablet/Mac and depth/parallax on TV reflect their platform focus models. ## Best practices Use system focus effects unless customization is essential. Do not move focus without input. If a focused item disappears during discrete directional navigation, move to a nearby one-step item; with other input, hide the indicator rather than guessing the next target. Follow platform reachability conventions: keyboard content focus on iPad/Mac coexists with Full Keyboard Access for all controls, whereas tvOS requires directional access to every interactive item. Use rings for text/search and usually full-row highlights for lists/collections. Standard focused/unfocused selection colors preserve active context. ## Platform considerations The source marks focus unsupported on iOS/watchOS in this topic’s sense. ### iPadOS Since iPadOS 15, Tab moves between focus groups and arrows move inside a group. Group custom views to produce expected reading order, normally leading-to-trailing then top-to-bottom; a vertical stack may need one focus-group container. Set priority so a likely primary item receives focus when a group is entered. Halo effects outline an item and can be refined for shape, clipping, or badge overlap. A content-configured cell’s highlighted accent appearance is separate from a focus effect. ### tvOS In full-screen content, gestures should act on the content rather than invisible focus. Use component focus for menus instead of a tiny free pointer; a gameplay-specific pointer must be conspicuous and integrated. Allow room and high-resolution art for enlarged focus states. Represent unfocused (receded), focused (raised/lit/moving), pressed (immediate feedback), selected (persistent choice such as filled favorite), and unavailable (inactive and unreachable) states distinctly. ### visionOS Connected keyboards/controllers use the same focus system family. Looking at content uses hover feedback instead; do not treat gaze hover as keyboard/controller focus. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Eyes Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/eyes) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Looking identifies a target in visionOS; system hover feedback signals that an indirect gesture can act on it. A tab can highlight before its bar expands to reveal labels, and a button may reveal a tooltip. Gaze before a tap remains private: the app does not receive its location. Connected-keyboard/controller focus is a separate system. ## Best practices Support assistive technologies and alternative input methods. Keep needed content within comfortable view; initial windows/volumes are placed by the system, while Full Space can request head-pose information for 3D placement. Avoid repeated large eye movements or rapid refocusing across depth. Sustained reading/content should normally sit at least 1 m away; close placement suits brief interactions only. Prefer standard components’ familiar hover responses. ## Making items easy to see Reduce noise, peripheral motion, and new content that pulls attention away from an intended target. Space items with at least a 16 pt margin around their bounds or at least 60 pt between centers. Avoid full-view repeating patterns/textures that can create ambiguous perceived depth; constrain them to smaller areas. ## Encouraging interaction Guide attention with centered placement and gentle contrast, color, scale, or movement instead of harsh flashing. Rounded shapes are easier to target than corners. For a single interactive object made of an image and label, define a containing hover region encompassing both. ## Custom hover effects Define normal and hovered appearances; the system applies them outside the app process and does not reveal current gaze/state or run gaze-dependent app code. A predefined favorite indicator can appear on hover, but hover cannot itself favorite an item. Reserve customization for distinctive moments. Use no delay for subtle affordances, a short delay when people may act quickly before expansion, and a longer delay for optional information such as tooltips. Keep at least one primary visual stable across states. Test on a worn Vision Pro for responsiveness, comfort, and distraction. ## Platform considerations This source is visionOS-specific and marks the other platforms unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/eyes) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 10, 2024, March 29, 2024, October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Remotes Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. The Siri Remote combines physical buttons and a touch-sensitive clickpad for tvOS navigation, selection, and playback across the room. ## Best practices Preserve standard gestures and focus direction outside specialized gameplay. Provide clear feedback connecting gesture to content. Presses indicate deliberate activation; resting/moving/passing the remote can cause accidental taps, so avoid acting on taps during live playback. Positional up/down/left/right taps can help only when intuitive and discoverable. Back normally opens the hierarchy’s parent, which is not always the previously visited screen; at the root it returns Home. During play, Back can open a pause menu to avoid accidental exits; Back from that menu resumes, while another deliberate action can return to the game menu. Holding Back reaches Home. Play/Pause must play, pause, or resume active media. ## Gestures Swipe scrolls with momentum based on swipe strength; vertical swipes along an edge accelerate through many items. Press activates or selects, and pressing before swiping enters scrubbing. ## Buttons Touch-surface swipe navigates/changes focus in apps and acts like a D-pad in games. Surface press activates/deepens navigation or acts as the game primary button. Back handles parent/exit or pause/resume according to context. Play/Pause controls media, while games may use it as a secondary action or to skip an intro. ## Compatible remotes For an app with an electronic program guide, guide/browse buttons open it; page-up/down navigate within it, also supported by upper/lower surface taps. Without an EPG, the system sends those requests to the default guide app. While content is playing, page-up/down should change channels rather than page through the guide. ## Platform considerations This source is tvOS-specific and marks the other five platforms unsupported. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance.

# Gestures Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Basic tap, swipe, and drag concepts work across touchscreens, air gestures, and input-device surfaces even though physical movements differ. ## Best practices Offer alternatives through voice, keyboard, Switch Control, or visible controls. Preserve standard gesture meanings rather than repurposing tap/swipe for unexpected actions. Give immediate, predictive manipulation feedback, including movement extent and unavailable/locked states. ## Custom gestures Add custom gestures only for frequent specialized tasks unsupported by standard ones. Make them discoverable, simple, distinct, and supplementary to another way to perform important actions. Explain them through simple words/graphics and test in real use; hard-to-explain gestures often need redesign. Keep standard navigation such as Back alongside shortcuts. Avoid system-edge/overlay gesture conflicts; specialized immersive/game contexts may defer system behavior using supported APIs. ## Platform considerations ### iOS, iPadOS Three-finger swipe left/right invokes undo/redo; three-finger pinch inward/outward copies/pastes selected text. Four-finger swipe switches iPad apps. Shake supports undo/redo. Simultaneous recognition can support games with concurrent movement/fire controls; integrate Pencil according to its specific guidance. ### macOS Keyboard and mouse are primary, with familiar gestures available on Magic Trackpad, Magic Mouse, and touch-enabled controllers. ### tvOS Preserve standard remote/Siri Remote/controller touch-surface gestures for navigation. ### visionOS Indirect input uses looking to target and a finger-thumb tap/hold/drag from rest; direct input physically touches nearby virtual objects. Prefer indirect UI interactions and reserve sustained direct work to avoid fatigue. Offer both where possible and alternatives to required posture/body movement. Direct touch activates; touch-and-hold reveals context; touch-and-drag moves; double touch previews or selects a word; swipe reveals/dismisses/scrolls; two-hand pinch apart/together zooms, and a two-hand circular pinch movement rotates. #### Designing custom gestures in visionOS Custom hand gestures require Full Space and hand-data permission. Test ergonomics repeatedly. Avoid sustained raised arms, repeated strenuous movements, complex finger/two-hand requirements, and a prescribed left/right hand; provide simpler alternatives. #### Working with system overlays in visionOS Since visionOS 2, looking at the palm and hand gestures reveal Home/Control Center; the older look-up behavior remains an accessibility option. Reserve the immediate hand/wrist region for these overlays, positioning any necessary hand-anchored game content farther away. In Full Space, supported deferral can require a tap before revealing Home, useful for virtual gloves/hands. Apps built for visionOS 1 defer by default. Rolling the hand/wrist/forearm conflicts with reserved overlays, which the app cannot detect and which appear above its content; test carefully. ### watchOS #### Double tap Since watchOS 11, double tap scrolls lists/views and advances vertical tabs. Do not assign a primary control that conflicts in those containers. On a non-scrolling view, designate the most frequent button/toggle, such as play/pause; the system highlights then acts. Widgets/Live Activities in Smart Stack can expose a primary action. Notifications use their first nondestructive custom action. ## Specifications ### Standard gestures Tap activates/selects, swipe reveals actions/dismisses/scrolls, and drag moves UI across all six platforms. Hold/pinch-and-hold exposes extra functions on every listed platform except macOS. Double tap zooms/toggles zoom across all six; the source specifically identifies Apple Watch Series 9 and Apple Watch Ultra 2 for the primary-action double tap. Zoom and rotate are listed for all except watchOS. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: September 9, 2024, September 15, 2023, June 21, 2023.

item.text: The brief identifies four problems: gaze opens details automatically, TV navigation requires pinpoint cursor movement, return loses focus, and Vision Pro actions require raised arms. The contracts will separate targeting from deliberate activation and preserve the gallery position on return.

name: apple-hig-foundations
description: Use when designing or reviewing Apple-platform visual hierarchy, accessibility, typography, color, Liquid Glass, layout, icons, imagery, motion, privacy, inclusion, localization, or spatial interfaces.
---

# Apple HIG: Perception, meaning and adaptable presentation

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the actual barrier or design decision: readability, visual hierarchy, imagery meaning, movement, locale, privacy or spatial placement. Choose the corresponding topic procedure rather than loading every foundation.
2. For text access, combine Typography with Accessibility only where size, reflow or reading alternatives matter. Use VoiceOver when grouping, semantics or navigation needs a procedure of its own.
3. For color/material decisions, separate content hierarchy from controls and evaluate the actual appearance/background/settings context. Preserve semantic meaning when appearance changes.
4. Deliver prioritized evidence-backed corrections or a concrete presentation specification. Distinguish inspected contrast/layout evidence from runtime and assistive-technology checks still needed.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Accessibility Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Shared gallery: Apple TV and Vision Pro interaction contracts

Design specification based on "'`interface.md`, not an implementation or device evaluation. The supplied gallery has 20 objects and details; no code, assets, dimensions, SDK versions, or runtime evidence were supplied. Object IDs below (`01`–`20`) are illustrative stable identities, not invented content names.

## Shared outcome and state

Browse all 20 objects, deliberately open one object'"'s details, then return to the same place. “Select” means activate to inspect details; this brief does not imply multiselect, favorites, or a new saved-selection feature.

Store "'`galleryOrder`, `originObjectID`, and `galleryScrollAnchor` before opening `Detail(objectID)`. Keep this gallery state while details are open. Merely targeting an object never opens details, changes stored selection, or marks it viewed. If viewed status is later added, derive it from explicit activation, never gaze.

Shared transition: `Gallery → explicit activation(id) → Detail(id) → Back → Gallery(origin id, saved anchor)`. A failed detail load retains the object title, a visible Retry action and Back; Retry loads the same ID. An empty gallery shows “No objects available” with an exit route rather than a phantom focus target. These are product decisions for predictable recovery.

## Contract 1 — Apple TV / tvOS

**Surface and entry.** Use a component-based gallery, not a free cursor. Proposed layout: five columns by four rows in the supplied order, with vertical scrolling if needed. On first entry, focus object 01. Each image and title is a single actionable card. Use standard tvOS focus effects and leave space for focused artwork enlargement without clipping or covering adjacent labels. Final card dimensions require asset/layout validation. Start from tvOS'"'s 66 × 66 pt default control size rather than designing to its 56 × 56 pt minimum. [Focus and selection — tvOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#tvOS), [Accessibility — Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Mobility).

**Directional route.** For row r, column c, Left/Right moves to the preceding/following card in that row; Up/Down moves to the same column of the adjacent row. Boundaries do not wrap. Scroll the newly focused card into view. Every card is reachable: 01 → Right ×4 → 05 → Down ×3 → 20; reverse navigation also works. No hidden controls or pointer precision are needed. Swipes follow the same directions with system scrolling/momentum; clickpad directional presses offer discrete navigation. This route is a proposed layout contract, not a claim about an existing focus engine.

| Input/state | Required result |
|---|---|
| Move remote focus | Change target and its visual emphasis only; remain in Gallery |
| Clickpad Select press on card | Immediate pressed feedback; capture ID/anchor; open that detail |
| Detail entry | Present object heading/content and a labeled Back to Gallery control; initial component focus goes to Back to Gallery |
| Back button or Back to Gallery | Return to parent Gallery; restore scroll anchor and focus to origin ID after layout is ready |
| Back at gallery root | Preserve normal system Home behavior; holding Back also retains system behavior |
| Play/Pause | Do not repurpose for opening details; if media is later introduced, control active media |

Remote meanings follow [Remotes — Best practices and Buttons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/remotes#Best-practices). Back follows hierarchy, not an arbitrary screen history.

**State appearance.** Unfocused cards recede; focused cards use the system raised/highlighted effect; pressed cards give immediate activation feedback. Any future persistent selected state uses a separate indicator that survives focus movement. Unavailable cards remain identifiable but inactive and skipped by directional focus. If the origin disappears while details are open, on explicit return choose the next available card in saved order, otherwise the previous; scroll to it. If none remain, show the empty state. During discrete navigation, removal of the focused card moves to a nearby one-step available target. These fallback choices are product rules applying [Focus and selection — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#Best-practices).

## Contract 2 — Vision Pro / visionOS

**Surface and entry.** Use an ordinary system-positioned window with a scrollable gallery and in-window detail navigation; this task needs no Full Space, head-locked UI, hand tracking, or custom gesture. Use four columns by five rows as an initial design, letting the window's layout expose fewer columns when needed. Keep the same object order and stable scroll anchor. The column count is a product proposal pending comfort testing, not a HIG requirement.

**Targeting is system hover.** Each image/title pair has one stable containing hit/hover region. Use standard rounded controls and subtle system hover; keep image, label and target bounds stable. Do not expand into neighbors or attach application logic to looking. Pre-tap gaze remains private and system-applied hover is distinct from connected keyboard/controller focus. Use at least 60 × 60 pt activation areas as the starting control size, with at least 16 pt margin around target bounds; verify final geometry at all supported layouts. The local eyes guide also offers at least 60 pt center separation as an alternative; this design chooses the margin rule. [Eyes — Making items easy to see, Encouraging interaction, Custom hover effects](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/eyes#Making-items-easy-to-see), [Accessibility — Mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Mobility).

| Input/state | Required result |
|---|---|
| Look at card | System hover feedback only; no navigation, stored state change, or dwell-to-open |
| Look and finger-thumb tap with hand resting comfortably | Explicitly activate targeted card; capture origin ID/anchor and open details |
| Standard indirect pinch/hold and drag to scroll | Scroll gallery with immediate visible movement; no card activation from scrolling |
| Activate visible Back to Gallery in details | Return in the same window; restore anchor and reveal originating card |
| Return under eye/hand input | No synthetic focus ring or forced gaze destination; hover follows the system's current target |
| Connected keyboard/controller navigation | Maintain a separate component-focus state; deliberate activation opens details; restore origin focus on return |

Prefer indirect interaction from rest. Direct touch may remain available through standard controls where appropriate, but no action requires reaching, raised arms, two hands, a prescribed hand, or body movement. Back is a visible labeled action rather than a custom wrist gesture; preserve palm/wrist system overlays. [Gestures — visionOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures#visionOS), [Gestures — Working with system overlays](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/gestures#Working-with-system-overlays-in-visionOS).

**Return and disappearance.** Restore content location, not eye focus. If the origin is removed, reveal the next available object in saved order, otherwise the previous, without inventing hover. For keyboard/controller focus, a removed target during discrete navigation uses a nearby one-step target; for other input, hide its obsolete indicator. Empty data uses the shared empty state. Keep details and Back within comfortable view without repeated broad gaze shifts or depth refocusing. Sustained reading should normally be at least 1 m away; rely on system placement and validate actual reading distance/comfort rather than claiming a fixed placement from this document. [Eyes — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/eyes#Best-practices), [Focus and selection — visionOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection#visionOS).

## Decisions across both contracts

- Replace auto-open with explicit activation. TV focus and visionOS hover identify possible targets; neither is a persistent product selection.
- Preserve object identity and scroll position across detail navigation. TV restores component focus; eye/hand Vision Pro restores the content location without manufacturing gaze or focus.
- Expose each card as one named action using its actual object title, role and availability. Expose Back to Gallery and Retry as named controls; provide meaningful descriptions for informative imagery without duplicating titles. Reading/task order follows gallery order, then the detail heading, content and actions.
- Support the entire browse/open/return task through supported assistive input, including Switch Control, and visionOS hand/head Pointer Control. Speech is optional. Connected keyboard/controller focus is a separate path from hover. These are requirements awaiting platform verification.
- Labels and state remain understandable without color or sound. Text enlargement to at least 200% must preserve all content/actions through reflow/scrolling; default text starting points are 29 pt on tvOS and 17 pt on visionOS. Reduce Motion retains targeting/pressed distinctions with restrained static emphasis instead of unnecessary zoom/depth animation. Validate actual contrast in supported appearances, including Increase Contrast. [Accessibility — Vision, Mobility, Cognitive and visionOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).

## Acceptance checks and evidence status

**Passed — document inspection only:** The brief was read. The two contracts preserve 20-object browsing and explicit detail activation; distinguish TV focus, visionOS hover and persistent selection; specify return restoration and removal/empty/error handling; provide remote and resting-hand routes. The finite TV route reaches all 20 proposed positions on paper. These are specification checks, not runtime passes.

**Failed — supplied concept, as described:** Looking opens details without deliberate activation; TV demands pinpoint pointer movement; return loses focus; Vision Pro requires raised arms. Each blocks or degrades the requested task and has a concrete replacement above. No implementation was inspected to confirm runtime defects.

**Not executed — required implementation/device checks:**

| Check | Observable pass criterion | Evidence still needed |
|---|---|---|
| TV browse/activate | Navigate every card and Back control with Siri Remote; focus is visible, never trapped; movement alone never opens details | Built app and actual remote/device recording; keyboard simulation is partial evidence only |
| TV visual feedback | Across-room labels are readable; enlarged focus art clips/obscures nothing; pressed and unavailable states are distinct | Final artwork, measured layout, TV viewing tests |
| TV return/removal | Open 01, 10 and 20, return via both routes; same ID and anchor restore; remove origin and verify fallback; root Back reaches Home | Runtime focus/scroll observations including delayed loading |
| Vision hover/activation | Sweep gaze across all visible cards without navigation or stored changes; deliberate tap opens only intended card; scrolling does not open it | Worn Vision Pro session and state/event inspection; no pre-tap gaze logging |
| Vision return | Open a scrolled-to object; Back restores location; eye input gets no artificial focus; keyboard/controller route restores its own focus | Device observations for each input path |
| Vision comfort/targets | Complete browse/open/return with resting hands; either hand works; targets remain separated and stable; no overlay conflict, repeated broad gaze or tiring reach | Measured geometry plus repeated worn-device comfort/recognition sessions |
| Recovery | Failed load offers usable Retry and Back; removed origin and zero available objects leave no stale target or dead end | Controlled runtime data/error fixtures |
| Accessibility | Complete the same task with platform-supported VoiceOver/Switch Control and visionOS Pointer Control/Zoom; names, order and activation are usable | Apple accessibility execution and Inspector results; supported input/platform matrix |
| Preferences/layout | At 200% text all titles/actions remain available; Reduce Motion preserves meaning; contrast passes measured chosen criteria in supported appearances | Rendered layouts, contrast measurements and preference execution |

No device, SDK compilation, GUI, accessibility, gesture-recognition, or physical-comfort testing was performed. Source support comes solely from the installed local HIG snapshot; official links above are attribution and were not browsed. No claims about newer releases or API availability are made.

## Local guidance audit

Read the installed "'`apple-hig/SKILL.md`, then `subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md`, then the `focus-and-selection`, `eyes`, `remotes`, and `gestures` topic `SKILL.md` files under that family'"'s "'`.topics/`, before their corresponding `references/*.md` source guides. For assistive alternatives, read `subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md`, its `.topics/apple-hig-accessibility/SKILL.md`, then `references/accessibility.md`. Every read used a separate `cat` command, with paths resolved from `/tmp/hig-eval-kpmt1ybf/.agents/skills/apple-hig`. The work used local files only.

- Replace auto-open with explicit activation. TV focus and visionOS hover identify possible targets; neither is a persistent product selection.
- Preserve object identity and scroll position across detail navigation. TV restores component focus; eye/hand Vision Pro restores the content location without manufacturing gaze or focus.
- Expose each card as one named action using its actual object title, role and availability. Expose Back to Gallery and Retry as named controls; provide meaningful descriptions for informative imagery without duplicating titles. Reading/task order follows gallery order, then the detail heading, content and actions.
- Support the entire browse/open/return task through supported assistive input, including Switch Control, and visionOS hand/head Pointer Control. Speech is optional. Connected keyboard/controller focus is a separate path from hover. These are requirements awaiting platform verification.
- Labels and state remain understandable without color or sound. Text enlargement to at least 200% must preserve all content/actions through reflow/scrolling; default text starting points are 29 pt on tvOS and 17 pt on visionOS. Reduce Motion retains targeting/pressed distinctions with restrained static emphasis instead of unnecessary zoom/depth animation. Validate actual contrast in supported appearances, including Increase Contrast. [Accessibility — Vision, Mobility, Cognitive and visionOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).
